item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
428
ABPZ20 KNHC 100519
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Wed Sep 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located well northwest of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Depression Fourteen-E, located several hundred miles
southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well South-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms located well to the
south-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands are associated with a broad
trough of low pressure. Some gradual development of this system is
possible late this week and into the weekend while it moves
generally northward and then meanders to the southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

Central Portion and West Portion of the East Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form several hundred miles
south of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula this
weekend. Gradual development of this system is expected thereafter,
and a tropical depression is likely to form early next week while it
moves generally westward over central and western portions of the
East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Fourteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Fourteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS INTO TROPICAL STORM NORBERT... As of 2:00 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 the center of Norbert was located near 16.4, -117.9 with movement W at 13 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1004 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 100841
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026
 
...DEPRESSION STRENGTHENS INTO TROPICAL STORM NORBERT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.4N 117.9W
ABOUT 685 MI...1105 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 16.4 North, longitude 117.9 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west near 13 mph (20 km/h). A westward to 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Some gradual strengthening is forecast over the next 
several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 100842
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
200 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026
 
The tropical cyclone appears to have become better organized
tonight. Earlier visible satellite images showed the low-level
center was fully exposed to the west of the associated deep
convection. Although westerly shear continues to affect the system,
recent proxy-visible satellite images show the center is likely
closer to or just underneath the edge of the cold overcast. Recent
AiDT and D-PRINT estimates from UW-CIMSS are in the 35-39 kt range,
and TAFB provided another 2.5/35-kt Dvorak classification. Based on
these developments, the system is upgraded to Tropical Storm Norbert
with an initial intensity of 35 kt.
 
Norbert is moving westward (280/11 kt) along the southern periphery
of a low- to mid-level ridge over the Eastern Pacific. This feature
will remain entrenched to the north of the system during the next
several days, which should keep Norbert on a westward to
west-northwestward heading through the 5-day forecast period. The
latest NHC track forecast is slightly slower and right of the
previous prediction at days 3-5, generally falling between HCCA and
Google DeepMind at those times. Otherwise, there were no notable
track changes made with this update.
 
The sheared structure of Norbert and the proximity of drier air to
the west of the system suggests that only modest near-term
strengthening should be expected. However, the shear is forecast to
weaken over the next few days while the system moves into a
sufficiently moist environment over 28-29C waters. Despite these
seemingly favorable conditions, there are mixed signals in the
guidance regarding how much strengthening may occur. Overall, the
intensity models trended weaker this cycle, and some minor
adjustments were made to the NHC intensity forecast to account for
this. However, the NHC forecast still lies on the higher end of the
guidance envelope and calls for Norbert to reach hurricane strength
by early next week.
